prerequisite: descriptive colony-ID continuity audit showing non-random code start/stop events on CHR and TOR
rationale: The complete-case V1 estimand failed its predeclared 75% retention validity gate because administrative/observational colony-code start-stop patterns remove otherwise informative trajectories. V2 changes the estimand rather than changing that gate: use all observed adjacent-year growth intervals without imputing missing codes or merging identifiers.

data.inclusion: retain colony codes with at least one positive reported count; never-positive administrative codes contribute no demographic trajectory and are excluded
data.missingness_rule: a growth interval exists only when the same colony_code is reported in both adjacent years; no missing value is treated as zero and no colony codes are merged or relabeled

primary_statistic.pairwise_growth_correlation: Pearson r between two colony-code annual log1p-growth series using their shared observed adjacent-year intervals
primary_statistic.minimum_overlap: at least 4 shared growth intervals, the smallest n giving positive Fisher-z information weight n-3
primary_statistic.weighting: Fisher z=atanh(r), weighted by n_shared-3; transform the weighted mean back with tanh separately for within-island and between-island pairs
primary_statistic.contrast: weighted Fisher-mean r within observed islands minus weighted Fisher-mean r between observed islands
primary_statistic.direction: two-sided primary test; positive contrast means colonies on the same island are more synchronous, negative means they are less synchronous

null.scheme: permute observed island labels within five fixed rank strata of each colony code's mean log1p abundance over its reported years
preservation: all colony trajectories and their missingness patterns
island label composition within abundance strata

validity: each observed island must have at least two included colony codes
the observed partition must have positive Fisher-information weight for both within-island and between-island pair sets
decision_rule: island demographic partition is supported for this overlap estimand only if the validity conditions pass and the empirical two-sided permutation p for the within-minus-between correlation contrast is <= 0.05
interpretation_boundaries: V1 remains formally invalid under its original 75% complete-case retention rule; V2 does not retroactively rescue it.
A positive V2 result shows that nominal island membership captures colony-level temporal covariance despite code start-stop patterns.
Without colony coordinates, V2 cannot distinguish coastline/island identity from geographic distance or other spatially structured island-level environments.
Covariance does not identify dispersal or individual movement.
Do not change overlap length, Fisher weighting, abundance strata, transforms, or permutation scheme after opening V2.
next_gate: If V2 is supported, freeze a GIS distance-conditioned test before opening colony coordinates. If unsupported, close the island-partition claim for Palmer rather than tune the overlap estimator.
